Bill number: HB1889
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1978
 By Akbari

 HOUSE BILL 1889

 By Hemmer

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 4,
 Chapter 29; Title 8, Chapter 44; Title 10, Chapter
 7 and Title 49, Chapter 6, relative to education
 freedom scholarships.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 35, is amended by

adding the following as new sections:

 49-6-3513.

 (a)

 (1) In compliance with all state and federal student privacy laws, the

 program is subject to audit by the comptroller of the treasury or the comptroller's

 designee. The audit may include a sample of scholarships to evaluate the

 eligibility of the participating students, the funds deposited in the scholarship

 accounts, and whether scholarship funds are being used for authorized

 expenditures. The audit may also include an analysis of the department's

 program monitoring process and the sufficiency of the department's fraud

 protection measures. The department shall cooperate fully with the comptroller

 of the treasury or the comptroller's designee in the performance of the audit. The

 audit must be made available to the members of the general assembly.

 (2) A private school that enrolls recipients is subject to audit by the

 comptroller of the treasury or the comptroller's designee. A private school shall

 pay for the cost of the audit and cooperate fully with the comptroller of the

 treasury or the comptroller's designee in the performance of an audit conducted

 pursuant to this subdivision (a)(2). The audit must be made available to the

 members of the general assembly and to the public on the comptroller's website.

 (b) A private school that enrolls recipients shall:

 (1) Voluntarily comply with the open meetings laws, compiled in title 8,

 chapter 44, part 1, and open records laws, compiled in title 10, chapter 7;

 (2) Provide a written report to the parent or legal guardian of a recipient

 of the recipient's educational progress at least twice each school year;

 (3) Not increase tuition for a recipient by more than ten percent (10%) as

 compared to the tuition charged to the recipient by the private school in the

 immediately preceding school year;

 (4) Annually disclose the admissions criteria, tuition rates, and

 demographics of the school on the school's website;

 (5) Annually disclose the admittance rate for the school for the respective

 school year; and

 (6) Publish the outcomes of the tests administered to recipients pursuant

 to § 49-6-3507 on the school's website.

 (c) The department shall require an eligible student to disclose the name of the

school in which the eligible student was enrolled in the immediately preceding school

year on the scholarship application in order to receive a scholarship.

49-6-3514.

 (a)

 (1) The department shall prepare an annual report for the program that:

 (A) Identifies each private school that enrolls recipients in the

 current school year;

 (B) Includes the number of recipients enrolled at each private

 school in the current school year;

 (C) Includes the outcomes of the tests administered to recipients

 pursuant to § 49-6-3507;

 (D) Identifies the county of residences for each parent or guardian

 who applied for a scholarship and whose student received a scholarship

 in the current school year;

 (E) Identifies the amount of scholarship funds each recipient

 spent in the immediately preceding school year and identify the types of

 allowable expenditures for which those funds were used by a recipient;

 (F) Reports the number of known violations of this part; and

 (G) Includes the annual reports submitted by each private school

 pursuant to subsection (b) for the immediately preceding school year.

 (2) The department shall submit the report to the general assembly and

publish the report on the department's website by October 1 of each year.

(b) Each private school that enrolls recipients shall:

 (1) Contract with a certified public accountant for the certified public

accountant to prepare an audit of the private school for each school year for

which the school enrolls recipients. The audit must examine and report:

 (A) The total amount of scholarship funds received by the school

 from enrolled recipients;

 (B) All expenditures made by the school that exceed twenty-five

 thousand dollars ($25,000); and

 (C) The name, title, and salary of each of the five (5) highest-paid

 employees of the school; and

 (2) Submit the audit prepared pursuant to subdivision (b)(1) to the

 department by August 1 of each year.

 49-6-3515.

 The comptroller of the treasury shall evaluate the program and submit a report to

 the general assembly by December 31, 2029, that includes the following information for

 the program based on data from the entirety of the program's existence for:

 (1) The educational outcomes of recipients;

 (2) The cost of administering the program; and

 (3) The effect of the program on LEAs, if any.

 49-6-3516.

 This part is repealed on July 1, 2030.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3504, is amended by deleting

subdivisions (c)(4) and (c)(5) and adding the following as a new subdivision (d)(4):

 (4) Be a member of a household with an annual household income for the

 previous year that does not exceed three hundred percent (300%) of the amount

 required for the student to qualify for free or reduced-price lunch, as provided in the

 income eligibility guidelines published by the United States department of agriculture's

 food and nutrition service.

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3507(a)(1), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting:

 (1) As a condition of receiving a scholarship pursuant to this part, a recipient

 must be annually administered the same Tennessee comprehensive assessment

 program (TCAP) tests, or successor tests authorized by the state board of education,

 administered to a public school student who is enrolled in the same grade or in the same

 course subject as the recipient.

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3507(a)(2), is amended by

adding the following at the end of the subdivision:

 A test administered to comply with subdivision (a)(1) must be uniformly

 administered to all recipients in the same grade level at the private school unless

 the recipient has an accommodation under the Individuals with Disabilities

 Education Act (20 U.S.C. § 1400 et seq.), or Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act

 (29 U.S.C. § 794).

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3508, is amended by deleting

subsection (b).

 SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-5101(a), is amended by adding

"and recipients, as defined in § 49-6-3502," after "all students" and adding "or the education

freedom scholarship program" after "Tennessee public school".

 SECTION 7. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-5101(c), is amended by adding

"and private school that enrolls recipients as defined in § 49-6-3502" after "each LEA" wherever

it appears in the subsection.

 SECTION 8. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would add income, testing, audit, and reporting rules to Tennessee’s education freedom scholarship program, beginning July 1, 2026. To qualify under a new provision, a student would have to live in a household whose income for the previous year did not exceed 300% of the amount required to qualify for free or reduced-price lunch under federal guidelines. Scholarship applicants would have to name the school they attended the previous year. The bill would also delete two existing subdivisions of the eligibility statute without showing their contents.

Scholarship recipients would have to take the same Tennessee comprehensive assessment program tests, or authorized successor tests, given to public school students in the same grade or course. A private school would have to administer a test uniformly to recipients in the same grade, except when a recipient has an accommodation under the cited disability laws. Schools enrolling recipients would have to give parents or guardians written progress reports at least twice a year, limit a recipient’s tuition increase to 10% over the prior year, publish specified admissions and school information and recipients’ test outcomes, and voluntarily comply with the cited open meetings and open records laws.

The comptroller could audit the program and private schools enrolling recipients. The education department and audited schools would have to cooperate; a school would pay for its audit. Schools would also have to obtain an annual audit from a certified public accountant covering scholarship funds received, expenditures over $25,000, and the names, titles, and salaries of their five highest-paid employees. They would submit those audits to the department by August 1. By October 1 each year, the department would publish and send the legislature a report covering participating schools, recipient counts and test outcomes, applicants’ counties of residence, prior-year scholarship spending, known violations, and school audit reports. The comptroller would report on recipients’ educational outcomes, program administration costs, and any effect on local education agencies by December 31, 2029. The bill would repeal this part of the law on July 1, 2030.

The bill would also delete subsection 49-6-3508(b) and add references to scholarship recipients, the program, and private schools enrolling recipients in two provisions of section 49-6-5101. The supplied text does not show the provisions being deleted or the surrounding language being amended.
</summary>

claims.claim: A private school may not increase a recipient’s tuition by more than 10% compared with the preceding school year.
claims.summary_quote: limit a recipient’s tuition increase to 10% over the prior year
claims.rationale: The bill sets the stated cap and comparison year.

claims.claim: Private schools enrolling recipients must publish specified admissions and school information.
claims.summary_quote: publish specified admissions and school information
claims.rationale: The required disclosures include admissions criteria, tuition, demographics, and admittance rate.

claims.claim: Private schools enrolling recipients must publish recipients’ test outcomes.
claims.summary_quote: publish specified admissions and school information and recipients’ test outcomes
claims.source_quote:
Publish the outcomes of the tests administered to recipients pursuant
 to § 49-6-3507 on the school's website.
claims.rationale: The bill requires publication of the specified test outcomes on the school’s website.

claims.claim: Private schools enrolling recipients must voluntarily comply with the cited open meetings and open records laws.
claims.summary_quote: voluntarily comply with the cited open meetings and open records laws
claims.source_quote:
Voluntarily comply with the open meetings laws, compiled in title 8,
 chapter 44, part 1, and open records laws, compiled in title 10, chapter 7;
claims.rationale: This is an express requirement for those private schools.

claims.claim: The comptroller or a designee may audit the program.
claims.summary_quote: The comptroller could audit the program
claims.source_quote:
the
 program is subject to audit by the comptroller of the treasury or the comptroller's
 designee.
claims.rationale: The program is expressly subject to such an audit.

claims.claim: The comptroller or a designee may audit private schools enrolling recipients.
claims.summary_quote: The comptroller could audit the program and private schools enrolling recipients.
claims.source_quote:
A private school that enrolls recipients is subject to audit by the
 comptroller of the treasury or the comptroller's designee.
claims.rationale: The bill separately makes those schools subject to audit.

claims.claim: The department must cooperate with a program audit.
claims.summary_quote: The education department and audited schools would have to cooperate
claims.source_quote:
The department shall cooperate fully with the comptroller
 of the treasury or the comptroller's designee in the performance of the audit.
claims.rationale: The department’s cooperation duty is express.

claims.claim: A private school must cooperate with a comptroller audit.
claims.summary_quote: audited schools would have to cooperate
claims.source_quote:
A private school shall
 pay for the cost of the audit and cooperate fully with the comptroller of the
 treasury or the comptroller's designee in the performance of an audit conducted
 pursuant to this subdivision (a)(2).
claims.rationale: The school’s cooperation duty applies to the audit under subdivision (a)(2).

claims.claim: A private school must pay for its comptroller audit.
claims.summary_quote: a school would pay for its audit
claims.source_quote:
A private school shall
 pay for the cost of the audit and cooperate fully with the comptroller of the
 treasury or the comptroller's designee
claims.rationale: In the surrounding discussion of comptroller audits, the bill assigns the school the audit cost.

claims.claim: Each private school enrolling recipients must arrange an audit for each school year it enrolls recipients from a certified public accountant.
claims.summary_quote: Schools would also have to obtain an annual audit from a certified public accountant
claims.source_quote:
Contract with a certified public accountant for the certified public
accountant to prepare an audit of the private school for each school year for
which the school enrolls recipients.
claims.rationale: The bill requires a CPA-prepared audit for each applicable school year.

claims.claim: The CPA audit must report total scholarship funds received from enrolled recipients.
claims.summary_quote: covering scholarship funds received
claims.source_quote:
The total amount of scholarship funds received by the school
 from enrolled recipients;
claims.rationale: This is a specified subject of the audit.

claims.claim: The CPA audit must report all school expenditures exceeding $25,000.
claims.summary_quote: expenditures over $25,000
claims.source_quote:
All expenditures made by the school that exceed twenty-five
 thousand dollars ($25,000);
claims.rationale: The threshold and expenditure scope match.

claims.claim: The CPA audit must report the names, titles, and salaries of the school’s five highest-paid employees.
claims.summary_quote: the names, titles, and salaries of their five highest-paid employees
claims.source_quote:
The name, title, and salary of each of the five (5) highest-paid
 employees of the school;
claims.rationale: The bill specifies these details for five employees.

claims.claim: Private schools must submit their CPA audits to the department by August 1 each year.
claims.summary_quote: They would submit those audits to the department by August 1.
claims.source_quote:
Submit the audit prepared pursuant to subdivision (b)(1) to the
 department by August 1 of each year.
claims.rationale: The deadline and recipient match the bill.

claims.claim: The department must publish and submit its annual report to the general assembly by October 1.
claims.summary_quote: By October 1 each year, the department would publish and send the legislature a report
claims.source_quote:
The department shall submit the report to the general assembly and
publish the report on the department's website by October 1 of each year.
claims.rationale: The bill specifies both actions and the annual deadline.

claims.claim: The department’s report must identify private schools enrolling recipients and the recipient count at each.
claims.summary_quote: covering participating schools, recipient counts
claims.rationale: Both items are required for the current school year.

claims.claim: The department’s report must include recipients’ test outcomes.
claims.summary_quote: recipient counts and test outcomes
claims.source_quote:
Includes the outcomes of the tests administered to recipients
 pursuant to § 49-6-3507;
claims.rationale: The report must include the specified test outcomes.

claims.claim: The department’s report covers counties of residence for scholarship applicants generally.
claims.summary_quote: applicants’ counties of residence
claims.rationale: The bill limits this item to parents or guardians who applied and whose student received a scholarship, not applicants generally.

claims.claim: The department’s report includes recipients’ scholarship spending in the preceding school year.
claims.summary_quote: prior-year scholarship spending
claims.rationale: The bill requires both amounts spent and types of allowable expenditures.

claims.claim: The department’s report includes the number of known violations.
claims.summary_quote: known violations
claims.source_quote: Reports the number of known violations of this part;
claims.rationale: The item is expressly required.

claims.claim: The department’s report includes the private schools’ submitted audit reports.
claims.summary_quote: school audit reports
claims.source_quote:
Includes the annual reports submitted by each private school
 pursuant to subsection (b) for the immediately preceding school year.
claims.rationale: Subsection (b) requires each school to submit its CPA audit; the department’s report includes those submissions.

claims.claim: The comptroller must report on recipients’ educational outcomes, program administration costs, and any effect on LEAs by December 31, 2029.
claims.summary_quote: The comptroller would report on recipients’ educational outcomes, program administration costs, and any effect on local education agencies by December 31, 2029.
claims.source_quote:
The comptroller of the treasury shall evaluate the program and submit a report to
 the general assembly by December 31, 2029, that includes the following information for
 the program based on data from the entirety of the program's existence for:

 (1) The educational outcomes of recipients;

 (2) The cost of administering the program; and

 (3) The effect of the program on LEAs, if any.
claims.rationale: The deadline and three specified subjects match the bill.

claims.claim: The bill repeals this part on July 1, 2030.
claims.summary_quote: The bill would repeal this part of the law on July 1, 2030.
claims.source_quote: This part is repealed on July 1, 2030.
claims.rationale: The repeal date is express.

claims.claim: The bill deletes subsection 49-6-3508(b).
claims.summary_quote: delete subsection 49-6-3508(b)
claims.source_quote:
SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-3508, is amended by deleting
subsection (b).
claims.rationale: Section 5 directs that deletion.

claims.claim: The bill adds references to scholarship recipients and the program in section 49-6-5101(a).
claims.summary_quote: add references to scholarship recipients, the program, and private schools enrolling recipients in two provisions of section 49-6-5101
claims.source_quote:
SECTION 6. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-5101(a), is amended by adding
"and recipients, as defined in § 49-6-3502," after "all students" and adding "or the education
freedom scholarship program" after "Tennessee public school".
claims.rationale: Section 6 adds the recipient and program references.

claims.claim: The bill adds a reference to private schools enrolling recipients in section 49-6-5101(c).
claims.summary_quote: private schools enrolling recipients in two provisions of section 49-6-5101
claims.source_quote:
SECTION 7. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-5101(c), is amended by adding
"and private school that enrolls recipients as defined in § 49-6-3502" after "each LEA" wherever
it appears in the subsection.
claims.rationale: Section 7 adds that reference to the second identified provision.

claims.claim: The supplied text does not reproduce the provisions being deleted or the surrounding language being amended.
claims.summary_quote: The supplied text does not show the provisions being deleted or the surrounding language being amended.
claims.rationale: The bill gives deletion and insertion instructions but does not reproduce the deleted provisions or the full surrounding statutory language.
